title: A multiplicative-group action on an affine scheme gives an integer grading
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $C$ a commutative $R$-algebra. For every commutative ring $A$, write $A[z,z^{-1}]$ for the ring of finite formal sums $\sum_{n\in\mathbf Z}a_nz^n$, with unique coefficients $a_n\in A$ and multiplication $z^nz^m=z^{n+m}$. Put $X=\operatorname{Spec}C$ and $G=\operatorname{Spec}R[z,z^{-1}]$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], with $G(B)=B^\times$ and multiplication of units for every commutative $R$-algebra $B$. Suppose an $R$-morphism $a:G\times_R X\to X$ [def-pc-fibre-product] satisfies the action identities $a_B(1,x)=x$ and $a_B(t,a_B(u,x))=a_B(tu,x)$ on all commutative $R$-algebras $B$, where $X(B)=\operatorname{Hom}_{R\text{-alg}}(C,B)$. Then there are $R$-submodules $C_n\subseteq C$, for $n\in\mathbf Z$, such that every $c\in C$ has a unique finite decomposition $c=\sum_n c_n$ with $c_n\in C_n$, the image of $R$ and $1_C$ lie in $C_0$, and $C_mC_n\subseteq C_{m+n}$. For every such $B$, every $x\in X(B)$, every $t\in B^\times$, and every $c\in C_n$, one has $a_B(t,x)(c)=t^n x(c)$. No finiteness, flatness, smoothness, field, or Noetherian hypothesis on $R$ or $C$ is required.

source.place: Tag 0EKK, lemma-complete-reducibility-Gm, with the action formula of Tag 0EKJ, example-Gm-on-affine. Relative version: the structural image of R has weight zero because the action is over Spec R.

proof.text: Put $L=C[z,z^{-1}]$, and let $i:C\to L$ be the constant inclusion. By [def-weil-affine-spectrum], $i$ gives an $L$-point of $X$; the pair $(z,i)$ gives an $L$-point of $G\times_R X$ by [def-pc-fibre-product]. Set $\rho=a_L(z,i):C\to L$, an $R$-algebra map. For any $R$-algebra map $h:L\to B$, composition of the corresponding maps of spectra with $a$ gives $h\circ\rho=a_B(h(z),h\circ i)$. In particular, the substitution $h_{t,x}(\sum c_nz^n)=\sum x(c_n)t^n$ is an $R$-algebra map for $t\in B^\times$ and $x:C\to B$, and $a_B(t,x)=h_{t,x}\circ\rho$. This naturality identity follows directly by precomposing the $L$-point with $\operatorname{Spec}h$; no representability comparison is being assumed.

source.place: Tag 0EKK, lemma-complete-reducibility-Gm, coefficient proof; Tag 0EKJ, example-Gm-on-affine, action formula. Relative version over R.

proof.text: For $c\in C$, define $p_n(c)$ to be the coefficient of $z^n$ in $\rho(c)$, so $\rho(c)=\sum_n p_n(c)z^n$ with finite support. Uniqueness of coefficients and $R$-linearity of $\rho$ imply that each $p_n:C\to C$ is $R$-linear. Apply the preceding substitution formula with $B=C$, $x=\mathrm{id}_C$ and $t=1$. The identity-action hypothesis gives $\sum_n p_n(c)=c$.

source.place: Tag 0EKK, lemma-complete-reducibility-Gm, coefficient proof; Tag 0EKJ, example-Gm-on-affine, action formula. Relative version over R.

proof.text: Take $D=C[w,w^{-1}][z,z^{-1}]$ and the constant inclusion $j:C\to D$. Apply $a_D(z,a_D(w,j))=a_D(zw,j)$ and the substitution formula of step 1. The left side, evaluated at $c$, is $\sum_n\sum_m p_m(p_n(c))w^mz^n$: indeed the inner point sends $d$ to $\sum_m p_m(d)w^m$, and the outer action substitutes that point on each coefficient of $\rho(c)$. The right side is $\sum_n p_n(c)w^nz^n$. Comparing the coefficient of $z^n$ first and then that of $w^m$ proves $p_m(p_n(c))=0$ for $m\ne n$, and $p_n(p_n(c))=p_n(c)$. Each double sum is finite since the outer sum has finite support and each coefficient has a finite Laurent expansion.

source.place: Tag 0EKK, lemma-complete-reducibility-Gm, coefficient proof; Tag 0EKJ, example-Gm-on-affine, action formula. Relative version over R.

proof.text: Define $C_n=\{c\in C:\rho(c)=cz^n\}$. These are $R$-submodules: both maps $c\mapsto\rho(c)$ and $c\mapsto cz^n$ are $R$-linear. The coefficient identities of step 3 give $\rho(p_n(c))=p_n(c)z^n$, so $p_n(c)\in C_n$. Step 2 therefore gives a finite decomposition of every $c$. If $\sum_n d_n=0$ is any finite sum with $d_n\in C_n$, applying $\rho$ gives $\sum_n d_nz^n=0$, and coefficient uniqueness gives every $d_n=0$. Subtracting two decompositions proves uniqueness.

source.place: Tag 0EKK, lemma-complete-reducibility-Gm, coefficient proof; Tag 0EKJ, example-Gm-on-affine, action formula. Relative version over R.

proof.text: Because $\rho$ is an $R$-algebra map, $\rho(1_C)=1_C$ and $\rho(r\cdot1_C)=r\cdot1_C$ for every $r\in R$, so $1_C$ and the structural image of $R$ belong to $C_0$. If $c\in C_m$ and $d\in C_n$, then $\rho(cd)=\rho(c)\rho(d)=(cz^m)(dz^n)=cdz^{m+n}$; hence $cd\in C_{m+n}$.

source.place: Tag 0EKK, lemma-complete-reducibility-Gm, coefficient proof; Tag 0EKJ, example-Gm-on-affine, action formula. Relative version over R.

proof.text: For any commutative $R$-algebra $B$, $x:C\to B$, $t\in B^\times$ and $c\in C_n$, step 1 yields $a_B(t,x)(c)=h_{t,x}(\rho(c))=h_{t,x}(cz^n)=x(c)t^n=t^nx(c)$. The substitutions and coefficient comparisons used only finite formal Laurent sums and the two given action identities; they imposed no further hypothesis on $R$ or $C$.
